AI has made it much faster to create an initial version of an app. Ask a coding agent to turn the spreadsheet your team uses to track supplier issues into an app, and it can be running in hours rather than days. Putting that app in front of the business is another matter. It needs a database, sign-in, and access to company data that respects the permissions already in place, and IT needs to know the app exists. Left to wire this up alone, an agent takes the shortest path, which often means copying data where it shouldn’t go or sharing it with people who shouldn’t see it. Multiply that by every team with an agent and you get shadow IT at agent speed. Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric apps address these deployment and governance challenges, and today at Microsoft Ignite, both are generally available. Developers and their agents build with Rayfin, our open-source SDK and CLI. items.title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide
items.excerpt: Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide . I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application. You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io : Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo. As an example, consider the following URL: https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/simonw/39fa5d399465766039549912e2b3d291/raw/f6dfba9

Our telemetry shows that agentic analytics has arrived. Agents query, investigate, iterate, test, and drill down without waiting for human input. This machine-paced activity pushes analytical engines built for human-paced workloads to their limits. Fabric Data Warehouse was built from scratch in the 2020s to support this new interaction model, combining highly scalable serverless compute, a resilient lakehouse architecture, and integration across Fabric. At Ignite, we’re building on that foundation for agents and the people who rely on them. The updates focus on performance at agentic scale, better interoperability with AI, and richer capabilities for warehouse development and operations. items.title: OneLake: The unified foundation for data, context, governance, and AI
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Most organizations' data is scattered across dozens of applications, clouds and services. Now that agents need to work across the entire business, organizations need to bring that data together in one place: one copy, open to every engine and team, without moving or duplicating it. Unified data gives agents reach, but to act with confidence they also need context: what the data means, how it connects to the business, who should see it and whether it can be trusted. OneLake is the single place for customers to unify their data estate. Shortcuts , mirroring , catalog federation and IQ Share bring multi-cloud, on-premises sources and databases and data platforms together into a single view of the data estate. The OneLake catalog provides a trusted place for organizations to easily explore, govern and secure data in OneLake. items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. AI is changing how every organization works. For most teams, the hard question isn't whether to use AI. It's how to turn it into real changes in daily operations: fewer surprises, faster responses, and better experiences for customers. Events often arrive faster than any person can respond. In the past, teams were limited by how quickly someone could read an alert and make a call. Now, agents can watch every signal and act in seconds, and each action and its outcome feed back into the system so it improves over time. This isn't only about factory floors or connected devices. Every organization has events it wants to respond to: Catch an issue before it happens, such as a shipment running late or a system nearing capacity. Monitor processes and systems for anomalies, enabling a fix before something breaks. Automate entire workflows instead of handing work between teams. items.title: Bringing trusted Fabric IQ context to wherever people and agents work
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Over the past year, AI has moved from answering questions to doing the work. As the 2026 Microsoft Work Trend Index shows, people are now handing entire tasks to agents and directing several at once. Those agents plan, decide, and act across systems, with less human review at every step. Fabric IQ helps turn your organization's business knowledge into an advantage for people and agents. As agents take on more responsibility, that knowledge matters more than which model they run on. Every organization can use the same frontier models. What sets yours apart is its context layer: the definitions, metrics, relationships, and rules that describe how your business actually works. When you connect that context with knowledge from across the organization, people and agents can uncover insights and take informed action that reflects how the business operates.
